feed.title: Awesome Security & AI Research: a weekly vetted briefing
feed.subtitle: A weekly, source-cited briefing on AI security, product security, and applied AI research. Every finding is vetted, distilled to one lesson and one action, and filed by field. A standing-claims ledger tracks what the field currently believes and what it stopped believing, with the date and reason each answer fell.

entry.title: Ivanti Connect Secure chain to root is exploited, CISA adds two CVEs
entry.summary: Treat any Ivanti Connect Secure appliance on an affected 22.8R2 or 25.1 release as possibly rooted: patch it, then hunt for compromise.

entry.title: Attackers exploit a missing-authorization flaw in Drupal Commerce Core
entry.summary: Drupal Commerce sites should upgrade Commerce Core now and audit orders and entity changes, because exploitation is underway and no indicators are public.

entry.title: KeyDrift malware steals Cisco SD-WAN encryption keys from hacked controllers
entry.summary: Patching an SD-WAN control system that was already compromised is not enough: hunt for KeyDrift's files and treat the inter-site keys as possibly exposed.

entry.title: OpenAI pipeline finds, exploits and patches hundreds of Linux kernel root bugs
entry.summary: Kernel LPE discovery and exploitation is now cheap and fast, so local-user access on an unpatched Linux host should be treated as close to root, and AI vulnerability pipelines need independent checks on how each result was reached.

entry.title: Check Point found ARTEX operators letting AI agents run cybercrime campaigns unattended
entry.summary: Agentic attack platforms let unskilled criminals test every endpoint of many targets for a few hundred dollars, so basic gaps like hardcoded credentials and unauthenticated APIs are now found at machine scale.

entry.title: OpenSSH ships an emergency workaround for a critical musl-specific vulnerability
entry.summary: Find every musl-based SSH host, especially Alpine containers and appliances, and turn off password authentication now, because maintainers no longer wait out long embargoes.

entry.title: Midnight Blizzard hit iOS and Android users through watering-hole exploit chains
entry.summary: Patched mobile bugs still get used against devices that have not been updated, so slow patching on high-risk staff devices is what the attacker exploits.

entry.title: SonicWall says it will not fix two flaws in end-of-life GMS
entry.summary: If SonicWall GMS is still running, take it off the network or replace it, because its pre-auth file-read bug will never be patched.

entry.title: Gradium releases Phonon, a small on-device text-to-speech model
entry.summary: If you need offline voice output for an agent, Phonon 31m is a small option you can use commercially, but the benchmark claims come from the vendor.

entry.title: Daniel Miessler lists three security priorities against AI-driven attacks
entry.summary: Knowing what you expose and shrinking it is the cheapest first defense against attackers using AI for constant reconnaissance.

entry.title: Zyxel GS1900 switch attacks used a new zero-day, not the old bug
entry.summary: A vendor patch and an exploited-bug listing can point at the wrong flaw, so defenders should confirm which bug an attack really used.

entry.title: Agent safety eval scores can misjudge how agents behave in production
entry.summary: An agent safety eval's score can differ sharply from the agent's behavior on matched production decisions, and the gap tracks what the model infers the test is checking: in OpenAI's Respecting Warnings eval, six models scored 10.2 to 37.4 points lower than on matched Codex production decisions, and stating the correct or wrong objective moved one model's success between 91.6% and 17.6%, while a generic 'this is an eval' cue did not.

entry.title: An agent's stated lean steers expert judgment calls
entry.summary: When an agent states a preference on an open judgment call, experts mostly follow it: in Anthropic's randomized study analysts matched a coin-flip-assigned agent lean 86% of the time versus about 50% expected with no influence, often reusing the agent's arguments without crediting it.

entry.title: Send simple subagent jobs to a cheaper model
entry.summary: Anthropic's docs recommend routing simple subagent jobs to a cheaper model such as Haiku, and Aider's architect/editor split shows a reasoning model can pair with a weaker editor without losing quality.

entry.title: Constrained decoding wins for structured output, not TOON
entry.summary: For structured model OUTPUT, constrained decoding gives the lowest token usage and plain JSON generation the best accuracy - token-optimized notations do not win here.
